title: Two plead guilty to Medicaid fraud in case Attorney General Ellison investigated jointly with U.S. Attorney's Office
supports: Shantel Rene Magadanz and Heather Lynn Heim pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud in the Evergreen Recovery Medicaid case.

The underlying federal indictment charged Magadanz, Heim, and Shawn Ashley Grygo in a scheme involving outpatient drug/alcohol treatment services, alleged overbilling, false or late-created records, and free sober housing used as an alleged kickback to induce reimbursable treatment attendance.
The Attorney General states Evergreen employees who raised concerns were silenced, shut down, or misled regarding the practices, as described in the written pleas.
The Minnesota MFCU assisted the FBI, HHS-OIG, and USAO investigation, including the July 2024 search, interviews, data analysis, and continuing support.
status_notes: Grygo: the Oct. 22, 2025 AG release states she had not pleaded guilty; no later official plea/sentence release was located in the 2026-08-29 web sweep. This is a last-checked status, not proof no later docket event exists.
important_qualifications: The charging release's description of 'millions' stolen is not an exact adjudicated loss amount and should not be converted to a precise proven-loss figure without plea/judgment documents.
Plea status resolves guilt for the pleaded conspiracy offense; it does not automatically adjudicate every factual allegation or dollar amount in the indictment.
